Convex is the backend platform that keeps up with you and your agents.

Our mission is to fundamentally change how software is built on the Internet by empowering developers to create fast, reliable, and dynamic apps without a backend team. We provide a full-stack app platform carefully designed with database, compute and backend abstractions that allow developers and LLMs to move fast but also create products that scale and remain simple over their lifetime.

The Team:

Convex has assembled a team that has built and designed some of the largest platforms in the world, and scaled companies to millions in revenue and thousands of employees. We’re a group of friendly, collaborative, and passionate people that love working in-person together in our office in San Francisco. We hire primarily in SF but have a few experienced folks working remotely in certain situations.

The Role:

Every week thousands of developers sign up for Convex, then start building and deploying on us. Some are kicking the tires. Some are quietly building the next big company. Your job is to help build the systems to find signal in the noise, and help us act. We’re looking for our first GTM Engineer to help us engage at just the right moment without being annoying about it.

You'll design, build, and ship the workflows and data infrastructure that turn product and market signal into pipeline, plus the internal apps and tools that compound our output. You'll walk in, audit what we have, decide what's missing, and start shipping.

Our users are developers, which makes this harder and more interesting than GTM engineering at most companies. Developers have antibodies against generic outbound, and the most valuable signal lives in product usage, not a lead form. We are deeply allergic to slop: the last thing the world needs is another ill-conceived cold email, and we won't ship one. Anything we send should be something a thoughtful person would be glad to receive. We’re not anti-AI by any means (helps us stay lean and move fast), and you'll be the person who keeps us on the right side of the line. The plays that work here are technical, specific, and earned, which is why we think the best version of this role is held by someone technical enough to build on Convex themselves.

What You'll Do:

  • Turn Convex product usage into the GTM signal it should be: model which deploys are getting serious, surface intent the moment a team crosses a threshold, and route it to the right play or the right human automatically.

  • Build agent + human-in-the-loop outbound that's genuinely useful, and keep it from ever becoming slop.

  • Build the AI agents and internal tools that compound the commercial team's output as we grow.

  • Audit the stack, generate your own backlog, and know when to reach for a point-and-click tool versus building something custom. Do the unglamorous data cleanup that makes all of it trustworthy.

  • Write a bunch of cool GTM code on Convex itself. We dogfood.

  • Measure your results and double down on what works best.

What Excites Us:

  • A few years spent building revenue and automation systems, whether you got there through Revenue Operations, Sales Ops, growth engineering, or as a software engineer who drifted toward the commercial side. You don't need "GTM Engineer" on your resume; the title barely existed a year ago, and we care far more about what you've built than what it was called.

  • Technical enough to build and wire systems together yourself. You don't have to be a career software engineer, but you're comfortable with APIs, data, and a bit of code (SQL, a scripting language, or TypeScript, which is what Convex itself is built in).

  • Hands-on experience inside a modern GTM stack.

  • Hands-on with AI in real work, not just in theory. You know where models are reliable and where they break, and you’re not afraid to fire up Claude Code or Codex to stand things up yourself rather than waiting on someone else.

  • Systems thinking: you consider what happens at 10x volume, when an API goes down, or when the same account hits your queue five times in parallel, and you design for it instead of leaving debt for someone else to unwind.

  • Bonus points for exposure to technical or developer-led sales motions, or genuine curiosity about Convex itself (building something small on it before you start wouldn't go unnoticed).

  • Interest in working in-person at Convex's office in SF.

Ideal Characteristics

This is an attempt to outline some characteristics of candidates who tend to thrive at Convex. We have a high demand for both commercial judgment and the ability to actually build, while also having the typical demands of a small startup.

Do they think in systems, not tasks?

The job is not to do GTM work faster by hand. It's to build the machine that does it. We want someone who, handed a recurring manual process, instinctively reaches for the version that runs itself. Someone who has built things that kept working after they walked away, and who measures their impact in leverage created, not hours logged.

Can they earn a developer's trust?

Developer tools are different. Your users are technical, skeptical, and quick to spot inauthenticity. The plays that work for a business app fall flat here. We want someone who understands, in their bones, what it feels like to be a developer evaluating a product, and who builds GTM motions that respect that instead of spamming through it.

Are they a commercially oriented builder?

The best GTM engineers we've met are hybrids: they care about revenue and they can ship. Not a marketer who can't build, not an engineer who doesn't care whether the work moves the business. We want someone who lives in the middle and is genuinely good at both.

Do they value simplicity and pragmatism?

Simplicity is at the heart of all good systems, and GTM systems are no different. Don't come here to build a Rube Goldberg machine of fifty chained automations. Come here because you want to get really good at achieving great things in the simplest possible way

Do they bring energy to the room?

Startups are hard. Building something from nothing is hard. Driving forward progress despite uncertainty is hard. Shitting on stuff is easy and just brings everyone else down. We have a high bar for quality but also a high bar for being constructive, positive, and excited about making things better. We're meant to be having fun here.

*The salary range for this full-time position is > $160,000 + equity + benefits

Convex is the backend platform that keeps up with you and your agents.

Our mission is to fundamentally change how software is built on the Internet by empowering developers to create fast, reliable, and dynamic apps without a backend team. We provide a full-stack app platform carefully designed with database, compute and backend abstractions that allow developers and LLMs to move fast but also create products that scale and remain simple over their lifetime.

The Team:

Convex has assembled a team that has built and designed some of the largest platforms in the world and scaled companies to millions in revenue and thousands of employees. We’re a group of friendly, collaborative, and passionate people that love working in-person together in our office in San Francisco. We hire primarily in SF but have a few experienced folks working remotely in certain situations.

The Role:

We have a real point of view and an obsession with craft. So far, this comes through mostly in our product. We need someone to own the creative identity of Convex and define what that looks and feels like. Our customers are developers, who can spot inauthenticity instantly. The brand has to be distinct, thoughtful, a little playful, and honest. The kind of thing a skeptical engineer trusts on sight.

The scope is broad. Brand, product design, marketing, events, the website: everything a developer encounters. The challenge isn't just doing the work, it's deciding what matters most. Convex is moving fast and there's more to own than any one person can cover, so the best person for this role is someone with the strategic judgment to prioritize ruthlessly and the conviction to hold a creative vision across a wide surface area.

This is a build-it-yourself role before it's a manage-it role. You'll be doing the work yourself, in Figma and in the codebase, working directly with the founders on brand and product. As we grow you'll hire a small, excellent group around you to scale your vision.

What You'll Do:

  • Set the creative strategy for how Convex shows up across brand and product, and make the calls on what to prioritize.

  • Own the Convex brand and identity across every touch point.

  • Do the work yourself now (alongside our existing team of creative freelancers), and build a small, world-class creative team later.

  • Set and hold the bar for taste across everything.

  • Keep us honest: kill the marketing BS before it ships, including ours.

  • Make a bunch of cool stuff.

What Excites Us:

  • A portfolio with range: brand systems and product design, not just one or the other.

  • Taste that's calibrated for a technical, skeptical audience and a track record to prove it.

  • The ability to set direction and also open the file and do the work.

  • The judgment to prioritize across a broad surface area and hold a creative vision while doing it.

  • Experience building or leading a small creative team.

  • Interest in working in-person at Convex's office in SF.

Ideal Characteristics

This is an attempt to outline some characteristics of people who tend to thrive at Convex. We have a high demand for taste, craft, and commercial instinct, while also having the typical demands of a small startup.

Do they have taste, with receipts?

We don't mean taste as an abstraction. We mean a track record of shipping things that are genuinely excellent, and a strong point of view on why they're good. Excellence can't be learned passively; we want to see the work and hear the reasoning behind it.

Do they think strategically about brand?

Great creative leaders have a point of view on where the brand should go, not just how to execute what's in front of them. We want someone who can look at Convex and form a clear opinion about what it should stand for visually, how it should evolve, and what it should never be. That conviction is what makes a brand coherent over time.

Can they execute and dream?

Strategy without execution is just theory. The best creative leaders we've seen can go from a brand direction conversation with a founder to opening Figma and making it real themselves. We need both, and we need them in the same person.

Do they get developers?

Developer tools are different. Positioning that works for a consumer app or a sales-led B2B product falls flat with engineers, who are quick to spot anything that doesn't ring true. We want someone who understands, in their bones, what it feels like to be a skeptical developer deciding whether to trust a tool.

Do they value simplicity?

The best design, like the best systems, is simple. We have a bias toward doing fewer things and doing them really well, and we want a creative leader who shares it: someone who can make a hard idea feel obvious and a complex surface feel intentional.

Do they bring energy to the room?

Startups are hard. Building something from nothing is hard. Driving forward progress despite uncertainty is hard. Shitting on stuff is easy and just brings everyone else down. We have a high bar for quality but also a high bar for being constructive, positive, and excited about making things better. We're meant to be having fun here.

*The salary range for this full-time position is > $250,000 + equity + benefits

A platform can be powerful and still fail if people don't enjoy using it. The surfaces developers interact with directly often dictate whether they stick around, no matter what happens underneath the hood. Building a product experience that's powerful, reliable, and genuinely enjoyable to use is still the domain of very talented humans, and we want you to be one of them.

 

The Team:

Convex has assembled a team of engineers who have built and designed some of the largest platforms in the world, with exabytes of data, millions of transactions per second, and shipped desktop and mobile software onto billions of devices. We are a group of friendly, collaborative, and passionate people that love working in-person together in our office in San Francisco. We hire primarily in SF but have a few experienced folks working remotely in certain situations.

The Role:

Convex’s product surface area is vast and includes our dashboard, insights, third-party integrations, project management, and more. These surfaces are core to our customers' businesses and need to be both powerful and delightful to use. We're looking for engineers who are deeply passionate about building good product experiences, especially as we grow more up-market.

This isn't a role for people who just want to solve puzzles. You'll apply product sensibilities to deciding "why" and "what" we build, not just "how". If you're an engineer with good design taste who cares about quality and enjoys working directly with customers to understand what they actually need, you'll likely be a great fit for this team.

What You’ll Do:

  • Design, build and maintain Convex's platforms, dashboard UI, integrations, and other services.

  • Work directly with customers and company leadership (hi! this is me, James) to shape plans for what features we need to build.

  • Projects you may work on in your first few months at Convex:

    • Design and build UIs for Convex Backend Components

    • Enhancing Convex's dashboard, CLI, and MCP to be world-class for AI agents

    • Upgrading Convex's role-based access control system to allow access tokens and integrations to have finer-grained permissions

What Excites Us:

  • 3+ years of professional software engineering experience.

  • Strong UX sensibilities and enthusiasm to build intuitive interfaces.

  • The ability to conceptualize the needs of someone else. Often our customers have much larger teams than ours with different business requirements we need to understand.

  • Experience or enthusiasm for scaling in a high growth startup environment.

  • Interest to work in-person at Convex's office in SF.

  • An ability to write high quality code and an enthusiasm for not being constrained to a certain layer of the stack

Ideal characteristics

This is an attempt to outline some characteristics of candidates that would make great engineers at Convex. We’re have a high demand for conceptual thought and architectural sensibilities, while also having the typical demands of a small startup.

Have they seen excellence?

If someone has a few years of experience it’s extremely valuable for them to have worked closely with a person, team or organization that’s truly excellent, in any domain. Excellence can’t just be learned passively since it requires being better than the status quo. The candidate doesn’t need to be excellent yet but they need to have an appreciation that it requires a lifetime of dedication.

Are they a deep thinker?

Convex is a rejection of industry norms and a belief there’s a better way of building apps. This requires us to think for ourselves and chart our own course. Engineers here need to think deeply about why they’re solving problems and the long-term implications of their choices. If someone does something just because they were told to or because it’s a “best practice” they will probably not excel here.

Are they obsessed with craft?

Craft is the difference between something that technically works and something people actually love to use, and it's most of what separates a good developer platform from a great one. We want an engineer who sweats the details most people would let slide, holds a high bar for how things feel to build with, and takes real pride in getting that last 10% right.

Do they value simplicity and pragmatism?

Simplicity is at the heart of all good systems, especially those that are able to scale and adapt to future needs. In addition to architectural simplicity, we also try to do the simplest thing to solve a given problem at Convex. Don’t come here because you want to write a consensus protocol or storage engine, even though sometimes we need to do these things. Come here because you want to get really good at achieving great things in the simplest possible way.

Do they bring energy to the room?

Startups are hard. Building something from nothing is hard. Driving forward progress despite uncertainty is hard. Shitting on stuff is easy and just brings everyone else down. We have a high bar for quality but also a high bar for being constructive, positive, and excited about making things better. We’re meant to be having fun here.

Do they have tenacity?

Working at Convex is rewarding and the workload isn’t crazy but our users come first and sometimes that means we need to be on-call. We sometimes (rarely), get paged at night and have to respond with dedication, sometimes need to dig deep to debug a tricky issue or solve a problem no one has solved before. There’s a camaraderie that comes from being in a team where everyone has tenacity, will step in to help each other out, and can be trusted to do the right thing.

*The salary range for this full-time position is >$180,000 + equity + benefits

Application demands are rapidly changing while the experience to design and operate infrastructure is rapidly diminishing. The Team:

Convex has assembled a team of engineers who have built and designed some of the largest platforms in the world, with exabytes of data, millions of transactions per second, and shipped desktop and mobile software onto billions of devices. We are a group of friendly, collaborative, and passionate people who love working in-person together in our office in San Francisco. We hire primarily in SF but have a few experienced folks working remotely in certain situations.

The Role:

We're looking for a Head of Developer Experience to own how developers and agents become great at building on Convex. You'll set the strategy, hold the point of view, and lead the team behind it. The docs, the writing, the developer narrative, and the advocacy your team takes to the community all flow from one thing: a real understanding of the product and a clear opinion on how people should build on it.

Some weeks you'll go deep with the engineering team on something we just shipped and turn it into docs a developer, or the agent writing their code, can pick up easily.   • Set the strategy and point of view for how developers and agents learn to be successful on Convex.

  • Craft the writing and developer narrative that shape how people understand Convex, from our blog to the way we explain what we ship.

  • Work closely with engineering and the founders to turn what we build into things people can learn from.

What Excites Us:

  • You've written developer docs or technical content that real developers relied on, and you have the work to show for it.

  • You've led a team before, ideally one doing developer-facing or content work, and know how to grow people and help them do their best work.

  • You can code, or read it closely enough to keep every example honest.

  • Genuine interest in how AI is changing the way software gets built, and a point of view on what developers and their agents need.

  • Interest in working in-person at Convex's office in SF.

This is an attempt to outline some characteristics of people who tend to thrive at Convex. We have a high demand for deep thinking and clear communication, while also having the typical demands of a small startup.

Writing is the heart of this job. We're not looking for someone who can produce serviceable copy, but someone who can take something complicated and make it clear, with a structure that scans and a point of view that sticks. It's the rarest thing we're looking for and the hardest to fake.

Do they have a point of view?

The best developer content and the best developer experience both come from someone who has a clear idea of what good looks like and pushes for it. We want someone who can look at how developers build on Convex today, form a strong opinion about how they should, and then build the docs, the writing, and the team to make that real.

Can they go deep technically?

You don't have to be the strongest engineer in the room, but you do have to engage seriously with the technical material and earn the team's trust. Convex is genuinely deep, and hand-waving doesn't survive contact with a skeptical developer. It shouldn't survive contact with you first.

Can they build and lead a team?

The best leaders we've worked with are the ones who make everyone around them better.

Convex is transforming the way developers build applications.

Our mission is to fundamentally change how software is built on the Internet by empowering developers to create fast, reliable, and dynamic apps without a backend team. We provide a full-stack app platform carefully designed with database, compute and backend abstractions that allow developers and LLMs to move fast but also create products that scale and remain simple over their lifetime.

 

The Team:

Convex has assembled a team of engineers who have built and designed some of the largest platforms in the world, with exabytes of data, millions of transactions per second, and shipped desktop and mobile software onto billions of devices. We are a group of friendly, collaborative, and passionate people that love working in-person together in our office in San Francisco. We hire primarily in SF but have a few experienced folks working remotely in certain situations.

The Role:

Convex is a backend platform but our key differentiator is an excellent client API and developer experience. We’ve invested huge efforts in our client libraries, development APIs and sync protocol to make Convex a joy to use for application developers. We’re looking to expand our team to develop the next version of the Convex API and help define what the modern application stack looks like.

If you’re an experienced TypeScript developer, care deeply about elegance and taste in API design, and believe that good platforms matter even more, not less, in an era of AI app development, then this is the job for you.

What You’ll Do:

  • Design, build, and maintain Convex’s client libraries, sync protocol, and query APIs.

  • Support new frameworks and keep track of new technologies in the app development space.

  • Develop an understanding of what abstractions scale and compose well in our stack so we can build libraries that are not just easy to use but also simple over the lifetime of a project.

  • Be self-directed to prioritize the right projects to work on, in close collaboration with the engineering team and CTO (hi! this is me, James).

  • Help establish good practices and design guidelines as we scale up our team and systems.

  • Write a bunch of cool client library code.

What Excites Us:

  • 3+ years experience building APIs, client libraries or developer tools.

  • Good understanding of best practices in the TypeScript, React, and web dev ecosystems.

  • Experience or enthusiasm for scaling in a high growth startup environment.

  • Interest to work in-person at Convex's office in SF.

  • Ability to write high quality code (strong TypeScript experience a plus).

  • An enthusiasm for going deep to understand Convex systems and not be constrained to a certain layer of the stack.

Ideal characteristics

This is an attempt to outline some characteristics of candidates that would make great engineers at Convex. We’re have a high demand for conceptual thought and architectural sensibilities, while also having the typical demands of a small startup.

Have they seen excellence?

If someone has a few years of experience it’s extremely valuable for them to have worked closely with a person, team or organization that’s truly excellent, in any domain. Excellence can’t just be learned passively since it requires being better than the status quo. The candidate doesn’t need to be excellent yet but they need to have an appreciation that it requires a lifetime of dedication.

Are they a deep thinker?

Convex is a rejection of industry norms and a belief there’s a better way of building apps. This requires us to think for ourselves and chart our own course. Engineers here need to think deeply about why they’re solving problems and the long-term implications of their choices. If someone does something just because they were told to or because it’s a “best practice” they will probably not excel here.

Do they understand the demands of a user-facing live-site service?

We generally weigh experience on OLTP databases over OLAP or offline systems. Not just because it’s more relevant domain experience but it also involves a mindset that the system absolutely must work because there’s a critical user-facing application on the other side. Live-site experience brings an appreciation of how hard it is to keep a service running at all times and how important it is to build simple well-abstracted systems that are less likely to fail.

Do they value simplicity and pragmatism?

Simplicity is at the heart of all good systems, especially those that are able to scale and adapt to future needs. In addition to architectural simplicity, we also try to do the simplest thing to solve a given problem at Convex. Don’t come here because you want to write a consensus protocol or storage engine, even though sometimes we need to do these things. Come here because you want to get really good at achieving great things in the simplest possible way.

Do they bring energy to the room?

Startups are hard. Building something from nothing is hard. Driving forward progress despite uncertainty is hard. Shitting on stuff is easy and just brings everyone else down. We have a high bar for quality but also a high bar for being constructive, positive, and excited about making things better. We’re meant to be having fun here.

Do they have tenacity?

Working at Convex is rewarding and the workload isn’t crazy but our users come first and sometimes that means we need to be on-call. We sometimes (rarely), get paged at night and have to respond with dedication, sometimes need to dig deep to debug a tricky issue or solve a problem no one has solved before. There’s a camaraderie that comes from being in a team where everyone has tenacity, will step in to help each other out, and can be trusted to do the right thing.

*The salary range for this full-time position is >$180,000 + equity + benefits

Application demands are rapidly changing while the experience to design and operate infrastructure is rapidly diminishing. A new platform abstraction is needed to support agentic development, agentic applications, and an entirely new set of application workloads. We think Convex is the team and platform best placed to define this abstraction.

Designing the platform, APIs, and frameworks for the future of application development is a difficult challenge. It requires a strong understanding of developer needs as well as the constraints that lead to applications that stay simple, correct, and secure over time. Building and leading the teams that make this possible is still the domain of very talented humans, and we want you to be one of them.

The Team:

Convex has assembled a team of engineers who have built and designed some of the largest platforms in the world, with exabytes of data, millions of transactions per second, and shipped desktop and mobile software onto billions of devices. We are a group of friendly, collaborative, and passionate people that love working in-person together in our office in San Francisco. We hire primarily in SF but have a few experienced folks working remotely in certain situations.

The Role:

We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead the teams that shape the Convex developer (and agent) experience. It's an ambitious and fast-moving mandate that spans a large surface area, from our development APIs, to agent frameworks, to integrations, to the component system that makes Convex effortless to build with. The unifying goal is simple to say and hard to do: be the best platform for developers, for building agents, and for agentic development.

This isn't a role where you hand off the technical work and manage from above. You'll help engineers understand why they're building what they're building, give them real ownership, and develop their judgment on how good something needs to be before it ships, all while staying in the architecture discussions and decisions about what to build and why. If you want to build a team that holds itself to a standard where 'it technically works' is never the finish line, you're going to like it here.

What You’ll Do:

  • Manage and grow the teams spanning our product experience, giving engineers real ownership and holding them to a high bar.

  • Develop a strong understanding of what developers and agents need from Convex and use it to make tradeoffs between competing priorities.

  • Work closely with our CTO and product lead to align the teams on priorities and make sure we're building the right things at the right time.

  • Stay hands-on technically, contributing to architecture decisions, code review, and technical direction.

  • Design, build, and maintain the developer-facing surfaces of Convex alongside the teams.

  • Give direct feedback and have hard conversations when they're needed.

  • Occasionally put up with James asking if there's a simpler more elegant solution to a problem.

What Excites Us:

  • Deep experience building and shipping high-quality developer-facing products or tools, ideally at a technical or developer tools company.

  • A track record of growing engineers and building strong teams, not just shipping software.

  • Genuine interest in how AI is changing the way software gets built, and a point of view on what developers and agents need from a platform like Convex.

  • Strong product sensibility and taste. You care about closing the gap between something that works and something that's a genuine pleasure to use.

  • Comfort with prioritization and tradeoffs across a broad surface area, and the judgment to know what matters for customers and what matters for the business.

  • Experience working in fast-moving environments where requirements shift and many of the hardest problems are not fully specified upfront.

  • Interest in working in-person at Convex's office in SF.

Ideal Characteristics

This is an attempt to outline some characteristics of engineering managers who tend to thrive at Convex. We have a high demand for conceptual thought and architectural sensibilities, while also having the typical demands of a small startup.

Are they deeply technical?

The best engineering managers we've worked with never really stopped being engineers. They have opinions about technical decisions, they can actually evaluate the work their team is doing, and they earn respect through judgment rather than a title on an org chart. If you can't get deep in the weeds with the team, you're going to have a hard time leading engineers who live there.

Do they develop people, not just ship software?

The job here isn't to be the best engineer on the team or to review every line of code. It's to give engineers real ownership, hold them to it, and help them get better over time. Sometimes that means stepping in, sometimes it means getting out of the way, and sometimes it means having a hard conversation nobody wants to have. A good manager knows the difference and takes responsibility for the team's outcomes either way.

Do they do it for the why?

At Convex, "my manager told me to" is not a satisfactory answer to why we're building something, even if the manager is the CTO. Engineers here don't just do things because they're told, they do them because they believe in them. A great EM spends the time to make sure the team understands the why, and when there's a disagreement, digs into the root of it rather than pulling rank.

Are they obsessed with craft?

Craft is the difference between something that technically works and something people actually love to use, and it's most of what separates a good developer platform from a great one. We want a manager who sweats the details most people would let slide, holds a high bar for how things feel to build with, and can pull that same standard out of the engineers around them.

Do they value simplicity and pragmatism?

Simplicity is at the heart of all good systems, and it turns out it's at the heart of good engineering leadership too. We want someone with a bias toward doing fewer things better, who pushes back on unnecessary complexity, and who knows when to tell the team to stop gold-plating something and just ship it because we're a startup and need to move.

Do they bring energy to the room?

Startups are hard. Building something from nothing is hard. Driving forward progress despite uncertainty is hard. Shitting on stuff is easy and just brings everyone else down. We have a high bar for quality but also a high bar for being constructive, positive, and excited about making things better. We're meant to be having fun here.

Are they worthy of trust?

Integrity underlies everything we do at Convex, and for a manager it matters even more. The team needs to trust that you'll be honest with them, go to bat for them, and do the right thing when no one is watching. Trust is hard to build and easy to destroy. We want someone who treats it as a way of life, not something you switch on when people are looking.

*The salary range for this full-time position is > $280,000 + equity + benefits

Application demands are rapidly changing while the experience to design and operate infrastructure is rapidly diminishing. A new platform abstraction is needed to support agentic development, agentic applications, and an entirely new set of application workloads. We think Convex is the team and platform best placed to define this abstraction.

Building infrastructure that’s fast, reliable, and designed to make good architecture easy and bad architecture hard is a difficult challenge. Building and leading the team that architects this platform is still the domain of very talented humans, and we want you to be one of them.

The Team:

Convex has assembled a team of engineers who have built and designed some of the largest platforms in the world, with exabytes of data, millions of transactions per second, and shipped desktop and mobile software onto billions of devices. We are a group of friendly, collaborative, and passionate people that love working in-person together in our office in San Francisco. We hire primarily in SF but have a few experienced folks working remotely in certain situations.

The Role:

We're looking for an Engineering Manager to lead our infra team, someone who is still very much an engineer. The team owns the database, the sync layer, and the newer primitives like branching and analytics that we're building out as they take shape, and a lot of this work has no playbook because we're the ones writing it. If you have a deep background in distributed systems and care about making the people around you better, we'd love to talk.

This isn't a role for someone who wants to step back from the technical work. You'll be working alongside the team on hard systems problems, contributing to architecture and code review, and working closely with our CTO on some of the most important technical decisions at the company. The leadership side is equally important: helping engineers think deeply about why they're building what they're building and giving them real ownership of hard problems. If you like the idea of guiding an engineer through designing a new storage layer, or helping the team set aside an interesting problem for a week to land something simple and pragmatic because we're a startup and need to ship, you're going to like it here.

What You'll Do:

  • Manage and grow the Infra team, giving engineers real ownership of hard problems and holding them to a high bar.

  • Work closely with our CTO to align the team on priorities and make sure we're working on the right things at the right time.

  • Stay hands-on technically, contributing to architecture decisions, code review, and technical direction.

  • Design, build, and maintain Convex's global cloud infrastructure alongside the team.

  • Investigate and improve the performance and reliability of our systems.

  • Help establish technical direction and engineering standards as Convex grows.

  • Give direct feedback and have hard conversations when they're needed.

  • Occasionally put up with James asking if there's a simpler more elegant solution to a problem.

What Excites Us:

  • Deep knowledge of distributed systems and operating infrastructure at scale, including owning systems through major scale transitions or building core infrastructure from scratch.

  • A track record of growing engineers and building strong teams, not just shipping software.

  • Strong systems judgment: understanding tradeoffs and knowing when to keep systems simple versus when to invest in complexity.

  • Experience working in fast-moving environments where requirements shift and many of the hardest problems are not fully specified upfront.

  • Interest in working in-person at Convex's office in SF.

  • Ability to write high quality code (knowledge of Rust is a plus, but you'll figure it out).

Ideal Characteristics

This is an attempt to outline some characteristics of engineering managers who tend to thrive at Convex. We have a high demand for conceptual thought and architectural sensibilities, while also having the typical demands of a small startup.

Are they deeply technical?

The best engineering managers we've worked with never really stopped being engineers. They have opinions about technical decisions, they can actually evaluate the work their team is doing, and they earn respect through judgment rather than a title on an org chart. If you can't get deep in the weeds with the team, you're going to have a hard time leading engineers who live there.

Do they develop people, not just ship software?

The job here isn't to be the best engineer on the team or to review every line of code. It's to give engineers real ownership, hold them to it, and help them get better over time. Sometimes that means stepping in, sometimes it means getting out of the way, and sometimes it means having a hard conversation nobody wants to have. A good manager knows the difference and takes responsibility for the team's outcomes either way.

Do they do it for the why?

At Convex, "my manager told me to" is not a satisfactory answer to why we're building something, even if the manager is the CTO. Engineers here don't just do things because they're told, they do them because they believe in them. A great EM spends the time to make sure the team understands the why, and when there's a disagreement, digs into the root of it rather than pulling rank.

Do they understand the demands of a user-facing live-site service?

We generally weigh experience on OLTP databases over OLAP or offline systems. Not just because it's more relevant but because it comes with a mindset: the system absolutely must work because there's a real user-facing application on the other side. A good infra manager has felt that weight themselves and knows how to build a team that takes it seriously, keeps a high bar for reliability, and builds simple well-abstracted systems that are less likely to fail in the first place.

Do they value simplicity and pragmatism?

Simplicity is at the heart of all good systems, and it turns out it's at the heart of good engineering leadership too. We want someone with a bias toward doing fewer things better, who pushes back on unnecessary complexity, and who knows when to tell the team to stop gold-plating something and just ship it because we're a startup and need to move.

Do they bring energy to the room?

Startups are hard. Building something from nothing is hard. Driving forward progress despite uncertainty is hard. Shitting on stuff is easy and just brings everyone else down. We have a high bar for quality but also a high bar for being constructive, positive, and excited about making things better. We're meant to be having fun here.

Are they worthy of trust?

Integrity underlies everything we do at Convex, and for a manager it matters even more. The team needs to trust that you'll be honest with them, go to bat for them, and do the right thing when no one is watching. Trust is hard to build and easy to destroy. We want someone who treats it as a way of life, not something you switch on when people are looking.

*The salary range for this full-time position is > $280,000 + equity + benefits

It’s not sufficient for Convex to be the best platform for agentic development, it also has to be the best platform for building agentic applications too, all while maintaining strong architectural principles that lead to applications that stay simple, correct, and secure over time. Architecting this platform is still the domain of very talented humans, and we want you to be one of them.

 

The Team:

Convex has assembled a team of engineers who have built and designed some of the largest platforms in the world, with exabytes of data, millions of transactions per second, and shipped desktop and mobile software onto billions of devices. We are a group of friendly, collaborative, and passionate people that love working in-person together in our office in San Francisco. We hire primarily in SF but have a few experienced folks working remotely in certain situations.

The Role:

We have a lot of work to do. The projects involve range from small ergonomic tweaks to make agentic development seamless, large structural changes like branching and automatic performance optimization of Convex projects, and keeping on top of and ahead of technological shifts in the industry.

The ideal candidate is an excellent engineer with the taste to develop composable APIs and abstractions, and the judgment to know when that's not the right call. This is a role with real latitude. You'll be looking at a broad product surface area, deciding what matters most, and building it without much hand-holding. If you're a former founder or an engineer who's comfortable moving between product and infrastructure, and you want to operate with a lot of autonomy on a small, high-leverage team, this is for you.

What You'll Do:

  • Work across our APIs, plugins, and AI framework integrations to make Convex the best platform for building agentic apps and agents.

  • Stay close to how developers are actually building with Convex, identify gaps, and own fixing them.

  • Be self-directed to prioritize the right projects to work on, in close collaboration with our Head of AI Ergonomics, the engineering team, and CTO (hi! this is me, James).

  • Strengthen the case that Convex is the best platform for agentic development, through demos, examples, and working directly with customers.

  • Write a bunch of cool code at the frontier of how AI apps get built.

What Excites Us:

  • 4+ years of experience shipping and owning developer-facing products, APIs, or tooling, with a track record of operating independently.

  • Strong instincts for what makes a developer tool feel right to use.

  • Genuine curiosity about how AI is changing the way software gets built.

  • Experience or enthusiasm for scaling in a high growth startup environment.

  • Interest in working in-person at Convex's office in SF, or have experience working remotely and be highly self-directed.

  • Ability to write high quality code (TypeScript experience a plus).

  • An enthusiasm for going deep to understand Convex systems and not be constrained to a certain layer of the stack.

Ideal Characteristics

This is an attempt to outline some characteristics of engineers who tend to thrive at Convex. We have a high demand for conceptual thought and architectural sensibilities, while also having the typical demands of a small startup.

Have they seen excellence?

If someone has a few years of experience it's extremely valuable for them to have worked closely with a person, team or organization that's truly excellent, in any domain. Excellence can't just be learned passively since it requires being better than the status quo. The candidate doesn't need to be excellent yet but they need to have an appreciation that it requires a lifetime of dedication.

Are they a deep thinker?

Convex is a rejection of industry norms and a belief there's a better way of building apps. This requires us to think for ourselves and chart our own course. Engineers here need to think deeply about why they're solving problems and the long-term implications of their choices. If someone does something just because they were told to or because it's a "best practice" they will probably not excel here.

Do they value simplicity and pragmatism?

Simplicity is at the heart of all good systems, especially those that are able to scale and adapt to future needs. In addition to architectural simplicity, we also try to do the simplest thing to solve a given problem at Convex. Don't come here because you want to write a consensus protocol or storage engine, even though sometimes we need to do these things. Come here because you want to get really good at achieving great things in the simplest possible way.

Do they bring energy to the room?

Startups are hard. Building something from nothing is hard. Driving forward progress despite uncertainty is hard. Shitting on stuff is easy and just brings everyone else down. We have a high bar for quality but also a high bar for being constructive, positive, and excited about making things better. We're meant to be having fun here.

Do they have tenacity?

Working at Convex is rewarding and the workload isn't crazy but our users come first and sometimes that means we need to be on-call. We sometimes (rarely), get paged at night and have to respond with dedication, sometimes need to dig deep to debug a tricky issue or solve a problem no one has solved before. There's a camaraderie that comes from being in a team where everyone has tenacity, will step in to help each other out, and can be trusted to do the right thing.

*The salary range for this full-time position is > $200,000 + equity + benefits
